text:
incident-bot: [P1] Runtime latency surge detected after canary rollout v2.14.0 — p95 up ~800ms in us-west-2, kernel fallback happening. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123

deploy-bot: Canary window: 12% hosts. Alerts: p95 > 400ms, tail errors ~0.2%. Rolling rule triggered.

alex: oncall alex — grabbing. Which customers/traffic slices affected?

maya: seeing spike concentrated on text-gen routes (/v1/generate). Kernel selector is falling back to older quant kernel on many hosts, causing smaller batches and CPU stalls. KV cache churn visible.

igor: this release included kernel-selector heuristics + prefetch tuning. if selector misclassifies seq lengths it can pick slower path. Recommend pause rollout and flip selector flag for canary.

alex: agreed. Can someone flip the FF for canary only? steps: `curl -XPOST https://ff.redwood/flags/kernel-selector-v2/toggle -d '{"env":"canary","value":false}'`

deploy-bot: feature flag `kernel-selector-v2` toggled OFF for canary at 1812345790 by alex. Rollout paused.

incident-bot: Routing fallback removed from canary hosts; monitoring 120s window.

lee: FYI CS: Customer-Delta (dedicated) reported timeouts and increased latency, they're opening a ticket. I'll patch them with status.

maya: after flip p95 on canary dropped from ~1.2s -> ~0.35s within 90s. KV miss rate still elevated on a subset — suggests cache warming + small-batch thrash. I recommend full canary rollback to be safe.

igor: agree with rollback. We'll revert to v2.13.9 for canary and re-run tests before re-rolling this kernel change. I'll own the postmortem.

alex: initiating rollback now. `@deploy-bot rollback --target canary --from v2.14.0 --to v2.13.9`

deploy-bot: Rollback to v2.13.9 initiated at 1812345835. Estimated completion 5m.

incident-bot: Customer impact summary: 3 customers showed latency degradation, no 5xx spike detected. No data plane forensics indicate SLO breaches yet. Downgrading to P2 for follow-up work once rollback completes.

maya: post-rollback metrics coming in: p95 restored to baseline, throughput normalized. We'll capture traces and a failing request sample.

igor: I'll open the postmortem and include: kernel-selector experiment, rollout gating, rollback playbook updates, and stricter canary thresholds for tail p95.

alex: Handoff: @igor leading RCA and follow-ups for next 4h. @maya to collect traces, @lee to continue customer comms. I'll stay on until stability confirmed. Close thread if stable in 30m. :white_check_mark:

igor: acknowledged. Creating postmortem doc and adding immediate mitigation action items (revert heuristic, add synthetic obs for slow kernels, refine ff rollout policy).

alex: thanks team. Monitoring window continues.
